newsitem.title: POLAND: Warta eyes new issue for 3 Polish banks.
newsitem.headline: Warta eyes new issue for 3 Polish banks.

text.p: Polish insurer TUiR Warta SA will on November 14 recommend to shareholders a new share issue for Bank Przemyslowo Handlowy SA (BPH), Kredyt Bank SA, Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK) and two minority shareholders, Warta said in a statement on Thursday.

In a draft resolution for an extraordinary shareholders meeting Warta said it planned to issue 865,380 to 2,596,139 registered shares to boost its capital, a move needed to continue expanding and restructuring its insurance portfolio.
It did not say how the shares would be divided, but said the executive board would set the price for them.

The new stock is due to be offered ex-rights to the three banks and Kulczyk Holding SA -- a company with interests as diverse as brewing and car dealing -- and one individual shareholder, Anna Wozniak.

Currently Warta has 3.46 million shares and its main stockholders are the state treasury, with a 34.7 percent stake, Elektrim with 10.1 percent, Anna Wozniak with 5.8 percent and Kulczyk Holding with 5.2 percent.

Warta said the capital increase was necessary to keep its own assets well above the solvency margin. It also said the new institutions could start playing the role of strategic investor for the insurer.

"Directing the issue to the above mentioned financially strong and stable entities means...not only an increase in the company's assets and higher security, but also allows the gaining of strategic shareholders," the statement said.
